extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders (policymakers, legal professionals, industry, researchers) searching Federal Register documents on climate disclosure and related regulations
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results page listing documents (rules, proposed rules, notices) matching the term “climate disclosure.” The page aggregates titles, abstracts, and short excerpts showing various regulatory and programmatic standards, reporting requirements, and procedural notices related to climate disclosure across multiple agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registrant climate-related disclosure requirement (SEC final rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Require registrants to provide certain climate-related information in their registration statements and annual reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final rules require information about a registrant's climate-related risks that have materially impacted, or are reasonably likely to have a material impact on, its business strategy, results of operations, or financial condition. The rules also require certain disclosures related to severe weather events and other natural conditions in a registrant's audited financial statements. Related headings on the document include: Content of the Climate-Related Disclosures; Presentation and Submission of the Climate-Related Disclosures; Safe Harbor for Certain Climate-Related Disclosures; Phase in Periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and presentation requirements for climate-related disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: The disclosure rules specify both the substantive content registrants must disclose and how disclosures must be presented and submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excerpt headings indicate separate treatment of the content (what to disclose), and presentation/submission (format and filing locations). The page references summaries and discussions (Overview and Purpose; Definitions of Climate-Related Risks) that frame how content and presentation are structured; the rules also discuss safe-harbor provisions and phase-in schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe harbor for certain climate-related disclosures (SEC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain climate-related disclosures may be covered by a safe-harbor treatment under final SEC rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The search excerpt lists a discrete Safe Harbor for Certain Climate-Related Disclosures as part of the Final Rules, indicating that some forward-looking or specified disclosures may receive safe-harbor protection; see related SEC guidance and the Final Rules for scope and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in periods and delayed effective dates
rubrics_metrics.description: Final rules and regulatory actions may include phase-in periods or delayed effective dates for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC Final Rules include Phase in Periods. Separately, an SEC document announces a delay of effective date pending judicial review (the stay is limited to the challenged Final Rules). EPA documents similarly extend deadlines for implementation of particular subparts (NSPS OOOOb, EG OOOOc). These mechanisms provide staggered compliance timelines or temporary delays while legal or administrative issues are resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: FAR proposed requirement: disclosure of GHG emissions and climate-related financial risk by major federal contractors
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed FAR amendment would require major Federal suppliers to publicly disclose greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related financial risk and to set science-based reduction targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DoD, GSA, and NASA proposed the FAR change to require major contractors to provide an annual climate disclosure aligning with TCFD recommendations, to inventory greenhouse gas emissions (Scope 1 and 2 and relevant Scope 3), and to set science-based targets. The preamble notes evolving industry practices and international regulatory landscape; a later entry withdraws the FAR proposal in a separate action when agencies judged insufficient time to finalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual climate disclosure aligning with TCFD (proposal/explanatory text)
rubrics_metrics.description: An annual climate disclosure is described as a set of disclosures by an entity that aligns with recommendations of the Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures (TCFD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The annual disclosure should cover the entity's current or previous fiscal year and include items recommended by the TCFD; the excerpt explicitly ties the disclosure concept in the FAR preamble to the TCFD framework and its recommended topics (governance, strategy, risk management, metrics/targets).

rubrics_metrics.name: GHG inventory requirements (Scope 1, Scope 2, and relevant Scope 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosures should include a greenhouse gas (GHG) inventory covering Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions and relevant Scope 3 emissions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FAR preamble language: 'The disclosure includes a GHG inventory of not only the Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, but also relevant...' and discussion notes that inventorying Scope 3 emissions may not be applicable to all significant contractors. Agencies discuss applicability and the burden of Scope 3 accounting in the regulatory preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for climate-related financial risk management for very large financial institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level principles to guide safe and sound management of exposures to climate-related financial risks for the largest financial institutions (those with over $100 billion in consolidated assets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The principles provide a framework covering supervisory approaches, time horizons for identifying materiality of climate-related risks, relationships between climate risks and other risks, tools and resources to manage and mitigate risks, scenario analysis, climate-related financial products, data and modeling challenges, and reporting and disclosure issues. They are intended to help large institutions focus on key aspects of climate-related financial risk management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information collection and reporting requirements for climate-related grant programs (EPA ICRs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant programs (e.g., Climate Pollution Reduction Grants, Transportation and Climate Division grant templates, Environmental and Climate Justice Community Change Grant Program) require specific information collection and reporting templates subject to OMB review under the Paperwork Reduction Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA published ICR submissions and requests for public comment; these notices describe new or revised reporting templates (post-award reporting, supplemental project application templates, project reporting templates) and solicit input on burden estimates and collection specifics. They signal mandatory reporting formats and schedules once approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carbon Dioxide Removal Purchasing Challenge criteria (DOE CO2RP Challenge)
rubrics_metrics.description: The DOE CO2RP Challenge will call on organizations to purchase small and growing quantities of high-quality, permanent carbon dioxide removal (CDR) credits and invites CDR suppliers to seek designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Challenge will coordinate with DOE prize programs; participating suppliers must deliver committed high-quality, permanent CDR credits to be eligible for prize awards or 'next wave' designation. The notice lists market barriers (insufficient incentives, policy and civil-society guidance gaps) the Challenge intends to address and frames evaluation in terms of demonstrated delivery of CDR credits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural and accessibility requirements for advisory committee meetings and public participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices for advisory committees and public meetings include procedural rules for participation, registration, agenda availability, and accessibility accommodations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include deadlines to register to attend, posting of final agendas in advance, provision of virtual attendance options, and instructions for requesting special accommodations. These procedural criteria govern how members of the public participate in advisory processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory authority and statutory-interpretation considerations for climate rules (EPA rescission example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory actions may hinge on statutory interpretation and application of doctrines (e.g., major questions doctrine) determining whether statutory provisions authorize specific greenhouse gas regulatory measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA rescission action states reasons why Clean Air Act section 202(a)(1) does not authorize the Agency to prescribe emission standards in response to global climate change concerns, citing interpretations of terms like 'air pollution,' 'cause,' 'contribute,' and 'reasonably be anticipated to endanger,' and invoking the major questions doctrine. Such legal-interpretation criteria affect whether and how agencies can implement climate-related standards.
